svg.aria-label: Hunter's Eye system map: the screen is captured three ways; thread 2 reads meters, belt, in-play and focus every frame while thread 3 reads item names with OCR; results go to lock-protected shared state; potions, auto-collect and hotkey sequences decide, pass a safety gate, and act through core/actions with mouse and keyboard, which changes the game and the next frame.
svg.text: A real-time, pixels-only vision engine. Python + OpenCV. Drawn from main at v0.020.

g.text: Every frame, all from that one small frame (about 5 ms)
Own thread and own full-size capture, so OCR never stalls the fast path
On an open inventory or stash?
then it's a tooltip, not a drop: skip
Transparent, click-through window over the game.
Draws the boxes and the F5 debug panel, repainted at most 30×/s.
On macOS it falls back to a plain debug window.
drawn on top of the game
Meter at or below a threshold: drink.
Keys are read off the belt.
Picks the best item on the ground
Far away? Teleport onto it first.
Click or cast until it's gone,
own thread, one at a time
quit, read the lobby's game name,
find itself on a stitched map, walk,
read the portal's label, go through,
fight whatever moves, and leave the
game below 20% health. F4 stops it.
own full-size capture for F3 and F7, only while one runs
if either says no, nothing acts
mouse & keyboard with real scancodes → the game reacts → the next frame shows it
read at startup · change behaviour without touching Python
potion rules, teleport key, timings, game name
what OCR looks for · line order = priority
where the orbs and potion belt are
reference art: in play, inventory, stash, Save and Exit
stitched maps + the path actually walked
